compiled_state.title: [CI llm-review pipeline]: reviewer reports cross-file consumer code as missing for 3 consecutive cycles -> repeating false positives block autonomous resolution
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
## Incident Overview

The CI `llm-review` job on PR #165 (https://github.com/navapbc/digital-service-orchestra/pull/165) has produced systematically-repeating false-positive findings across 3 consecutive cycles. The pattern is consistent and indicates the reviewer is not receiving the full cross-file diff context when constructing findings, despite being instructed to review the whole diff.

## Specific evidence

### Repeat false positive 1 — `origin_main_sha consumer not visible`

`finding_id: f-a1b2c3d4` (cycle 3 — third recurrence)

Reviewer claim: "New state field `origin_main_sha` is captured and stored but the comment claims it is `Used by --resume freshness check` — however, no consumer code is visible in the diff. The diff shows merge-to-main-direct.sh was modified (index hash changed) but contains no visible content changes."

Reality: the consumer IS in the SAME commit (`6c305025af`), located in `plugins/dso/scripts/merge-to-main-direct.sh` at the `--resume` block around line 935+. The code reads `origin_main_sha` from the state file, fetches `origin/main`, runs `git merge-base --is-ancestor`, and resets `completed_phases` on staleness. Verified by:
```
grep -n "origin_main_sha\|merge-base --is-ancestor" plugins/dso/scripts/merge-to-main-direct.sh
```
which returns multiple hits. Test coverage exists (`tests/scripts/test-merge-to-main-resume-freshness.sh`, 6 passing tests).

Despite a PR-thread defense reply pointing at the consumer file, the SAME false positive resurfaced in subsequent cycles — suggesting the reviewer either does not load defenses or its diff window does not include the consumer file.

### False positive 2 — `Lock file behavior documented but not implemented`

`finding_id: f-e5f6g7h8` (cycle 3)

Reviewer claim: "the concurrency model docstring claims flock-style locking at /tmp/merge-to-main-lock-<shasum>, but grep reveals no lock file creation, flock calls, or mutual-exclusion implementation."

Reality: lock IS implemented in `merge-to-main-direct.sh` around line 348+: `LOCK_FILE="/tmp/merge-to-main-lock-$(echo -n "$MAIN_REPO" | shasum ...)"`, `_wait_for_lock`, `_acquire_lock`, `_release_lock`. The function `_is_lock_stale` is defined in `merge-helpers.sh`. **25 tests** in `tests/scripts/test-merge-to-main-locking.sh` cover this code path and all pass. The docstring added in PR #165 only describes the existing mechanism.

### False positive 3 — `Test file truncated`

`finding_id: f-i9j0k1l2` (cycle 3)

Reviewer claim: "the diff introduces a new test file at tests/scripts/test-merge-to-main-resume-freshness.sh, but the diff ends immediately after the file header (only shows new file mode 100755). No test assertions, helper sourcing, or test functions are visible."

Reality: the file is 138 lines and has 6 passing tests. Verified by `bash tests/scripts/test-merge-to-main-resume-freshness.sh` returning `PASSED: 6 FAILED: 0`. Either the diff payload was truncated before reaching the reviewer or the diff parser silently dropped the file body.

## Hypothesis

The reviewer pipeline either:
1. Truncates the diff at a size threshold without warning, dropping content past some line/byte cap;
2. Uses a per-file diff window that excludes cross-file references — so a reviewer looking at `merge-helpers.sh` cannot see the consumer in `merge-to-main-direct.sh` even when both files are in the same commit;
3. Does not honor PR-thread defenses (the cycle-1 defense reply for the same finding was ignored in cycles 2 and 3);
4. The context-augmentation loop (`review.context_aug.*`) is either not firing or not fetching the cited consumer files.

## Reproduction

PR #165 cycles 1, 2, 3 all triggered llm-review with the same diff. Cycle 2 and 3 added additional commits but the original two commits (5d49a2338d, 6c305025af) were unchanged. The false positive about `origin_main_sha consumer not visible` appears in EVERY cycle.

## Impact

P2 — autonomous resolution loop cannot converge when the reviewer systematically cannot see the consumer code for state fields. PRs requiring cross-file feature implementation (state init in one file, consumer in another) will be blocked by repeating false positives. `review.max_resolution_attempts=3` is exhausted on PRs that are correctness-clean.

## Recommended investigation areas

- `dso_ci_review/runner.py` and how the diff is constructed before being passed to the model
- `review.context_aug.*` config keys — verify the context-augmentation loop is being invoked; check `docs/contracts/ci-review-context-request.md`
- Whether `review-github-defense-store.sh` defenses are being loaded into the cycle-N+1 prompt
- The mirror-defenses-to-pr.sh wrapper: are the cycle-1 defenses visible to the cycle-2 reviewer?
- Diff size / line caps: is there silent truncation past N lines or M bytes?

## Workaround

Bypass llm-review (admin merge) when the failing findings can be evidenced as false positives via PR-thread defense, until this is fixed.

## Links

- PR #165: https://github.com/navapbc/digital-service-orchestra/pull/165
- Parent epic for cb31-3552 hardening: (open) cb31-3552-8c22-4416

comments.body:
## Confirmed root cause: region-split fallback fragments cross-file context

**Evidence**: PR #165's actual diff against its base (`6b09ee219b`) is **688 LOC across 7 files**, exceeding the `_LOC_THRESHOLD = 400` in `plugins/dso/scripts/dso_ci_review/region_split.py:25`. This triggers the region-split fallback (Strategy E, story f5f9-9a3c).

The fallback partitions the diff into **per-directory clusters** via `_cluster_files()` (region_split.py:63-90). For this PR the clusters are:

| Cluster | Files |
|---|---|
| `plugins/dso/hooks/lib/` | merge-helpers.sh (state-field initialization site) |
| `plugins/dso/scripts/` | merge-to-main-direct.sh (state-field consumer), merge-to-main-pr.sh |
| `tests/scripts/` | 4 test files |

Each cluster is dispatched to a separate specialist that sees ONLY its cluster's hunks. The arch-synthesis pass then merges findings — but a finding emitted by the hooks/lib/ specialist ("consumer not visible") is preserved into the synthesis without being reconciled against the scripts/ cluster which DOES contain the consumer.

**Validated against the three repeating false positives:**

- `f-a1b2c3d4` "origin_main_sha consumer not visible" — state field initialized in hooks/lib/merge-helpers.sh, consumer in scripts/merge-to-main-direct.sh. Different clusters → consumer invisible to the cluster-1 specialist that emitted the finding.

- `f-e5f6g7h8` "lock not implemented" — concurrency docstring added to scripts/merge-to-main-direct.sh as a head-comment. Lock implementation is also in scripts/merge-to-main-direct.sh (lines 348+) but the docstring at the top is a separate diff hunk than the lock code further down. Likely the specialist's diff-window for the scripts/ cluster was further truncated, dropping the lock hunks.

- `f-i9j0k1l2` "test file truncated, only file-mode line visible" — direct evidence that per-file content was truncated in the diff payload delivered to the tests/scripts/ cluster specialist.

## Why prior defenses didn't suppress

`_fetch_pr_defenses` (runner.py:636) does fetch defenses from PR comments, but defense matching uses cited_lines proximity (±5-line window) inside `_apply_defenses` (runner.py:864-913). When the cycle-N+1 specialist re-emits the same finding from a different cluster with potentially different cited_lines, the proximity match misses, the finding is treated as new, and the defense doesn't fire.

## Recommended fixes (for follow-up epic)

1. **Cross-cluster consensus before emit**: arch-synthesis pass should re-check any finding citing 'consumer not visible' / 'not implemented' against the FULL diff (all clusters), not just the cluster that emitted it.
2. **Context-augmentation on cross-file findings**: when a specialist emits a 'missing X' finding, run the context-augmentation loop to fetch X from siblings before the finding is finalized.
3. **Cluster boundary metadata in prompt**: tell each specialist 'you see cluster A; clusters B/C exist; do not emit "missing" findings for symbols you cannot see — emit a context_request instead'.
4. **Defense lookup by description hash**: in addition to cited_lines proximity, match defenses by normalized description text — the same false positive will recur with the same wording even when cited_lines differ.
5. **Region-split threshold tuning**: 400 LOC is low for refactors with companion tests. Consider raising or factoring test-file LOC separately.

## Reproduction

```
cd /Users/joeoakhart/digital-service-orchestra-worktrees/worktree-20260516-093623
git diff 6b09ee219b..HEAD --stat   # 688 LOC, 7 files
git diff 6b09ee219b..HEAD | grep -c -E '^[+-][^+-]'  # 688 (over 400 threshold)
```

Region-split is confirmed to fire on this diff. Cycle-3 CI run: https://github.com/navapbc/digital-service-orchestra/actions/runs/25971678287/job/76344010186

comments.body: /dso:fix-bug BASIC investigation: confirmed root cause per ticket comment — region-split fallback fragments cross-file diff context into per-directory clusters; arch-synthesis does not reconcile 'missing consumer' findings across sibling clusters. Classification: COMPLEX. Fix requires (1) cross-cluster consensus check in arch-synthesis before emitting 'missing X' findings, (2) context-augmentation on cross-file 'missing' claims, (3) cluster boundary metadata in specialist prompts, (4) defense lookup by description-hash. Multi-subsystem: region_split.py, runner.py, arch-synthesis agent. Not suitable for single-bug fix-bug pass; recommend /dso:brainstorm seed. Leaving OPEN.
